_note: Every value here is adjustable. 'src' says where it came from; ESTIMATE means no public figure was found and the value is a reasoned estimate. Re-run closure_model.py after editing.

structural_gap.src: ESTIMATE (central of $25-45M): FY28 structural gap. FY27 GF adopted $734.7M (budget.mpschools.org, June 9 2026) closed a $39.7M gap with recurring cuts; drivers (3-4% comp growth on ~$580M staff vs 2-3% formula growth) continue. No published FY28 figure as of Oct 2026.

revenue_per_pupil.src: ESTIMATE from FY27 MPS budget: marginal revenue lost/gained per student = basic formula $7,683/APU (FY27) + referendum ~$2,140 + compensatory if eligible; range $10-13.5k. City Auditor rule of thumb ~$10k.

variable_cost_share.src: ESTIMATE (revised Oct. 9, 2026 after review): blended marginal cost of an added or lost student. About 30% of revenue follows a student who fills a seat in an existing class (supplies, services, some aide time). A student who forces a new class also needs about 1/25 of a teacher plus 0.2 FTE specialist (about $6,000, another 52% of revenue). Recruits cluster at K entry and popular schools; assuming about 40% need new classes gives 30% + 0.4 x 52% = about 51%, used as 50%. Previous value 0.30.

teacher_loaded.src: MPS FY27 average teacher incl. ~37.7% fringe (budget book); used for specialists, interventionists, counselors and social workers (counselor $136k, SW $127k)

office_loaded.src: MPS FY27 average school secretary, loaded

utilities_per_sqft.src: MPS deck slide 111: Option 1 removes ~1.0M operating sq ft (8.2M -> 7.2M) for $635,000/yr utility savings

maintenance_per_sqft.src: ESTIMATE: routine maintenance/repairs avoided on a mothballed building; mothballing still costs ~$0.40/sqft (security, minimal heat), netted below

mothball_cost_per_sqft.src: ESTIMATE: cost of keeping an unprogrammed building secure and heated

sqft_per_custodian.src: MPS deck slide 111: current sq ft per custodial FTE

custodial_savings_share.src: ESTIMATE: deck assumes custodial staffing is redeployed to raise cleaning level; we count half as savings

one_time_closure_cost.src: ESTIMATE: moving, IT, signage, receiving-school prep per closed building (one-time, amortized over 5 years in net figures)

elementary.src: ESTIMATE: blended K-5 section cap under MFT contract class-size targets

staff_floors._doc: FTE required per building = max(floor, enrollment / students_per_fte). Encodes the 'MPS student experience' floors from deck slides 84-90.

distance_source.src: Oct. 10, 2026: road miles and driving minutes along the fastest route on the street network (OpenStreetMap roads via Overture Maps, release 2026-09-23.1; school addresses geocoded to Overture address points). Built by tools/routing/ and stored in data/compiled/school_drive_matrix.csv. 'straight_line' restores the earlier map-distance method.

cost_per_rider_fixed.src: Calibrated so an average rider (~2.5 road mi) costs ~$3,850/yr: MPS $73M (2024-25) / ~19,000 daily riders

cost_per_rider_mile.src: Calibrated with the fixed term to MPS average $3,850/rider/yr

circuity.src: Routed trips between schools average 1.40 x the straight line (median; Overture/OpenStreetMap roads, Oct. 2026). Still used for the home-to-school legs the routing does not cover (attendance radius, magnet home distance) and to put routed trips on the straight-line scale of the per-mile attrition and walking coefficients. Earlier ESTIMATE: 1.35.

attendance_radius_mi.src: ESTIMATE: mean home-to-school distance in a K-5 attendance area (~2.5 sq mi per area)

share_riding_now.src: ESTIMATE: share of community-school students currently bused (outside 0.5 mi walk zone)

spare_rider_capacity.src: ESTIMATE: new riders that fit on existing routes before new buses/routes are needed

congestion_multiplier.src: ESTIMATE: marginal cost multiplier for riders beyond spare capacity (new routes, driver-shortage premiums, longer tiers)

max_ride_mi_before_premium.src: ESTIMATE: beyond this one-way road distance a dedicated route is needed

long_ride_premium_per_mi.src: ESTIMATE: extra annual cost per rider per mile beyond the threshold

attrition._doc: Students lost = direct (displaced students) + spillover (whole-district confidence). Both grow non-linearly with the number of closures N.

direct_base.src: Chicago 2013 closures: ~6% of displaced students left the district (UChicago Consortium); +2 pts for Minneapolis's dense charter/open-enrollment market (42% of residents already outside MPS, 2022-23)

direct_growth_per_closure.src: ESTIMATE: displaced families more likely to leave as more schools close (N=15 -> ~20% direct)

direct_per_extra_mile.src: ESTIMATE: +4 pts leave rate per extra mile to the new school

split_body_penalty.src: ESTIMATE: +4 pts when a school community is split across receivers

pathway_break_penalty.src: ESTIMATE: +6 pts when students must leave their current high school pathway

spillover_scale.src: ESTIMATE: share of ALL remaining students who leave = scale * N^2.2 (N=15 -> ~2%, ~500 students). Local evidence: MPS 2021 redesign (no closures) coincided with >4,200 students (>10%) leaving in two years

spillover_exponent.src: ESTIMATE: confidence collapse is strongly convex

max_combined_enrollment.src: ESTIMATE: 3 specialists rotating half-days can cover ~28 sections (~700 students) across two buildings

fte_saved_per_pair.src: User ask: specialists split half days at two schools; two 3-FTE floors become one shared 3-FTE team

max_travel_minutes.src: ESTIMATE: a midday transfer longer than ~15 min, including parking and setup, costs a teaching period and is impractical

avg_speed_mph.src: Used only when transport.distance_source is 'straight_line'. With routing, minutes come from the drive-time matrix (median about 18 mph between schools under 3 road miles apart, about 28 mph across all pairs).

fixed_transfer_minutes.src: ESTIMATE: parking, sign-in, setup (added to the routed driving time)

growth_protect_threshold.src: User ask: preserve schools in areas with large projected growth (10-yr change map). Communities >= +15% protected: Central, Phillips, University, Longfellow, Near North, Northeast

protect_comprehensive_hs.src: User ask: preserve current high school pathways

receiver_capacity_basis.src: Workbook 'Modeled Future Design Enrollment' upper bound

receiver_growth_reserve.src: Receivers keep room for their community's projected 10-yr growth

extended_curve_max.src: Extension to show where costs explode

pathway_overrides.src: Reviewer and Jordan (Oct 8, 2026): return Kenwood to the Southwest High pathway it fed before the 2021 redesign. Southwest has 1,170 students in a building designed for 1,959-2,177 (workbook), so it has room.

protect_neighborhood_middle.src: Anwatin is the walkable neighborhood middle school for Kenwood and Bryn Mawr (1.1 and 0.2 road mi). Closing it sends Kenwood 6-8 students to Franklin in North Minneapolis (3.0 mi) or to Anthony (5.7 mi). Kept open so Kenwood's path is Kenwood - Anwatin - Southwest.

district_option_splits.src: District Options 2 and 3 send Kenwood-area students through Anthony Middle to Southwest; North Bryn Mawr goes to Franklin and North (Ward 7 News, Sept. 18, 2026; North News, Sept. 27, 2026). Kenwood share of Anwatin = Kenwood K-5 / (Kenwood + Bryn Mawr K-5) = 370 / 767 = 0.48. ESTIMATE

middle_ground_closures.src: Policy (Jordan, Oct. 10, 2026): Middle Ground is locked at 5 closures. The within-5%-of-peak rule below is now a check, not the selector (it picks 5 under routed central assumptions, by about $8,500). Set to null to let the rule choose.

optimum_tolerance.src: Floor on the tolerance below, in $ a year (the earlier rule, Oct 8, 2026).

optimum_tolerance_share.src: Policy (Jordan, Oct. 10, 2026): pick the fewest closures whose net savings are within 5% of the peak. Net savings are flat from 5 to 9 closures (within $0.6M a year, under 2% of the $35M gap), and the plan aims for as few closures as possible.

receiver_max_share_of_mps_design.src: Policy (added Oct. 9, 2026 after Minneapolis Families for Public Schools' review): a receiving school may be filled to at most 90% of its design enrollment in MPS's 2024 Physical Space Study (the figure on MPS's public building reports), leaving room for growth and for programs. MPS rates 70-90% 'efficient'.

recruitment._doc: Used by levers.py. Turns the recruitment lever into a cost and a risk so the three plans can be compared on all three levers.

base_cost_per_recruit.src: Florida pay-per-recruit enrollment contracts 2025-26: $935-985 per student enrolled (research_finance_sources.md section 8); rounded up

volume_half_point.src: ESTIMATE: average cost per recruit rises linearly with volume as easier families are reached first; cost doubles at 8,000 recruits

trust_sensitivity.src: ESTIMATE: each 1% of district enrollment lost to spillover (loss of confidence) raises recruiting cost 25%; families who watched neighboring schools close are harder to win back

amortization_years.src: ESTIMATE: recruited students stay several years; one-time campaign cost spread over 5 years

district_baseline_recruits.src: District deck slide 95: enrollment strategies project ~28,000 K-12 students in 2030-31 and 2035-36, i.e. roughly flat; no net growth beyond today

underdelivery_test.src: Stress test: recruitment delivers only 60% of target

resident_pool.src: MPS deck slide 96: residents in charters 13,389 + open enrollment out 6,685 + nonpublic 4,814 + homeschool 460

evidence_pace_pct.src: Saint Paul Public Schools 2024-25: +2% (~600 students) in its best recent year (state Oct 1 count), aided by immigration; Detroit 2025 +1.1%. No urban precedent found for >3%/yr from recruitment alone (case_studies_other.md)

stretch_pace_pct.src: Stretch: stacks pre-K3/4 pipeline (DC lottery study: +16.8 pts K enrollment for Pre-K3 winners), identity/dual-language programs (SPPS +16-58% at those schools), re-enrollment metrics, and no further closures

capacity_response._doc: Added Oct. 9, 2026 at Jordan's request: the net value of each added student depends on how full the district's open buildings are on average (enrollment / column N design enrollment, after closures and departures).

full_benefit_until_util.src: Policy choice (Jordan): below 80% average utilization each recruit is worth the full net revenue ($5,750).

taper_end_util.src: Policy choice (Jordan): from 80% to 90% the value falls as more recruits must be bussed to buildings with room; at 90% new classrooms or buildings are needed.

bus_cost_per_added_rider.src: MPS transportation about $73M (2024-25) / about 19,000 daily riders = $3,850 a rider a year. Phased in linearly from 80% to 90% utilization.

new_capacity_cost_per_seat.src: ESTIMATE: reopening a closed elementary of about 450 seats: staffing floors (principal, office, specialists, interventionists, social worker) about $1.27M + building operations about $0.30M + reopening cost $0.6M over 5 years ($0.12M) = about $1.7M a year, or about $3,800 a seat. Applies to every recruit above 90% utilization, on top of busing.
